search_intent: Compare FOB and CIF quotations for Chinese vehicles shipped to a Middle Eastern destination
editorial_angle: Middle East FOB and CIF quote verification should link Gulf conformity, Arabic customs files, port charges and registration to the same VIN list.

sources.title: Frequently Asked Questions on Customs Valuation

sources.title: Mutabiq User Guide
sources.supports: The GSO user guide lists vehicle conformity authentication, fuel economy labels, recall registration and VIN registration. Its authorized-importer item is explicitly for motorcycles, not evidence of car-importer eligibility.
sources.verification_scope: Official GSO documentation was read via the browser research tool; the Mutabiq shortcut points to www.gso.org.sa. This is a system-scope check, not verification of a particular certificate or destination acceptance.

evidence_gaps: The Middle East is not one customs or vehicle-approval territory, and even GCC conformity does not replace each state's import, tax, inspection, insurance and registration controls.
Current ocean freight, terminal, documentation, storage, testing, inland and banking costs require live quotes for the named port and importer.
The exact GSO certificate scope, model year, variant, VIN batch, authorised applicant and national acceptance must be authenticated for the vehicles offered.
CIF insurance details, battery-electric treatment, used or repaired condition, transshipment, territorial limits, deductibles and Arabic claims support require policy review.
Customs valuation and vehicle-condition evidence can be tested by national authorities, so no supplier amount or duty estimate is guaranteed.

editorial.purpose: Help international vehicle buyers make safer, evidence-led sourcing decisions.

evidence.note: No first-hand inspection, transaction, interview or ownership claim is made.
